_method_note:
(recorded in the pack and in research_gaps):
  PREMISE CHECKS. Five premises in the originating brief were checked against primary sources
  before any row was written. The checks follow the findings_memo §1 practice: corrections are
  recorded, not applied silently.
    1. "Gotham (law enforcement)" - NOT the official positioning. palantir.com/platforms
       describes Gotham as "The Operating System for Global Decision Making ... for operators
       across roles and all domains". Documented law-enforcement use is real but sits in US
       deployments (ACLU: New Orleans predictive policing 2018; ICE ICM/ELITE 2025-26), not in
       the platform's marketed identity. No Australian police deployment was found (RG-093).
    2. "'Pre-crime' arrest capabilities" - a characterisation from the GNCA video, not a
       product claim by Palantir or NVIDIA. The nearest VERIFIED Australian fact is the WA
       Police real-time facial recognition trial (launched 2 Jul 2026, 19 arrests in week one,
       vendor not disclosed) - which is NOT a Palantir system on any evidence found. The two
       must not be merged (RG-093).
    3. "Apollo (cloud infrastructure)" - officially "The Operating System for Continuous
       Delivery" ("from the back of a humvee to the hull of a submarine"). Cloud delivery is
       part of it; the official identity is continuous deployment across environments.
    4. The Jensen Huang quote - the circulating short form "accelerate everything that
       Palantir does" is the GNCA video description's paraphrase. The verified keynote wording
       (Sherwood News transcript, GTC Washington DC, 28 Oct 2025) is: "We work with Palantir to
       accelerate everything Palantir does so that we can do data processing at a much much
       larger scale and more speed - whether it's structured data of the past, human-recorded
       data, unstructured data - and process that data for our government, for national
       security, and for enterprises around the world". Verification against the keynote
       recording itself is RG-092.
    5. "AI-as-weapon systems" - an interpretation. The pack records the primary-sourced facts
       that an editorial layer may weigh: Maven designated a US program of record for
       weapons-targeting AI (Reuters, Mar 2026); the UK MoD's own release describing Palantir
       work on the "kill chain" and targeting (gov.uk, Sep 2025); the UN Special Rapporteur's
       "reasonable grounds" finding on Palantir support to the Israeli military (A/HRC/59/23,
       via Al Jazeera). The interpretation itself is not a row.
  SUPPLIER-ENTITY ANOMALY. Three AusTender notices name PALANTIR TECHNOLOGIES AUSTRALIA PTY
  LTD (ABN 48 144 948 309, Canberra) as supplier; the ASD notice CN3992202 names the US
  parent PALANTIR TECHNOLOGIES INC. (Denver, ABN "Exempt"). Which legal entity holds which
  Australian deployment - and where each one's data sits - is RG-087.
  DATE DISCREPANCY. Crikey (17 Feb 2026) states ASD granted Palantir "a top security
  clearance" in November 2024. Palantir's own primary announcement of IRAP PROTECTED is
  20 Nov 2025. IRAP assessment is not a personnel/facility security clearance. Unresolved;
  RG-089. Both claims are recorded as sourced, neither as fact.
  MONEY. AusTender values are recorded as published (inc GST per AusTender convention).
  Non-AUD figures live ONLY in metrics with explicit units (USD m, GBP bn); gov_contracts and
  ownership keep the AUD rule.

sources.title: Palantir and NVIDIA Team Up to Operationalize AI - Turning Enterprise Data Into Dynamic Decision Intelligence (NVIDIA newsroom release, GTC Washington DC)
sources.notes: The partnership's founding release. Palantir integrates NVIDIA accelerated computing, CUDA-X libraries and open Nemotron models into the Ontology at the core of Palantir AIP; NVIDIA Blackwell coming to AIP; 'Enterprises will be able to run AIP in NVIDIA AI factories'; AIP supported in the NVIDIA AI Factory for Government reference design announced the same day; Lowe's first customer for supply-chain optimisation. Huang quote: 'Palantir and NVIDIA share a vision: to put AI into action, turning enterprise data into decision intelligence.' Karp quote on fusing Palantir decision intelligence with 'the world's most advanced AI infrastructure'.

sources.title: AI Infrastructure and Ontology - Under the Hood of NVIDIA and Palantir (Palantir Blog)
sources.notes: Palantir's own account of the 28 Oct 2025 announcement: Jensen Huang announced the partnership in Washington DC; deliverables listed as Nemotron Super (49B reasoning model) on Palantir secure cloud infrastructure via the Palantir Model Catalog, NeMo Retriever in Foundry Pipeline Builder / Code Workspaces / Ontology Toolchain, and cuOpt optimisation. Links the GTC DC keynote recording (youtube.com/live/lQHK61IDFH4) at t=5114s as the announcement moment - the timestamp cited in RG-092.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang announces new partnerships with Palantir, CrowdStrike, Uber (Sherwood News, markets)
sources.notes: Contemporaneous transcript of Huang's GTC DC remarks. Called Palantir Ontology 'the single fastest enterprise company in the world and probably the single most important enterprise stack in the world today', and: 'We work with Palantir to accelerate everything Palantir does so that we can do data processing at a much much larger scale and more speed - whether it's structured data of the past, human-recorded data, unstructured data - and process that data for our government, for national security, and for enterprises around the world, process that data at speed of light and find insight from it.' This is the verified long form of the quote the originating brief paraphrased.

sources.title: NVIDIA, US Tech Leaders Unveil AI Factory for Government Reference Design (NVIDIA blog)
sources.notes: The government-facing half of the 28 Oct 2025 announcement: full-stack AI infrastructure reference design for federal agencies and regulated industries, built on Blackwell (RTX PRO Servers, HGX B200), Spectrum-X, BlueField, Nemotron, designed for FedRAMP-authorised clouds and high-assurance environments. Palantir AIP integrates with it; CrowdStrike, ServiceNow, Astris AI (Lockheed Martin) and Northrop Grumman are in the same design. Establishes that the partnership ships as a hardware-software stack for government 'high-assurance' environments, not only enterprise analytics.

sources.title: Palantir Launches Engine for Deploying NVIDIA Nemotron Open Models in Sovereign Environments (Palantir investor release)
sources.notes: Phase two of the partnership, focused on US government agencies and critical infrastructure: deployment engineering for base and customised Nemotron models in 'classified, air-gapped, and other sensitive environments'; model engineering letting agencies 'change the weights of the models themselves'; telemetry-driven post-training loop ('customers will own self-improving models specific to their mission'); delivered through the joint Palantir Sovereign AI Operating System Reference Architecture (palantir.com/sovereignaios). Karp: many US clients 'already using these models, including multiple supporting critical US infrastructure - both private and public'. Huang: 'Open source AI is foundational to national security, public safety and U.S. technology leadership.'

sources.title: NVIDIA and Palantir Bring Sovereign Intelligence to Critical Supply Chains (NVIDIA newsroom release)
sources.notes: Phase three: NVIDIA deploys Palantir Foundry/AIP + post-trained Nemotron models on its OWN supply chain ('from wafer to first token'; 1.3 million parts per Vera Rubin rack). Runs on the jointly developed Palantir Sovereign AI Operating System Reference Architecture (SAIOS), supported by Dell and Cisco; deployable on-premises, in colo and cloud (Rackspace, Nebius). Huang: 'Supply chains are the operating system of the physical economy, and AI factories are among the most complex systems ever built.' Karp calls the partnership 'cornerstone' of Palantir's 'sovereign AI revolution'. The NVIDIA-Palantir stack is now exportable to any organisation wanting supply-chain AI on infrastructure it controls - the deployment pattern relevant to Australian sovereign-AI buyers.

sources.title: NVIDIA Expands AI Infrastructure Capacity in Partnership With Australia's Data Center Ecosystem (NVIDIA newsroom release)
sources.notes: NVIDIA collaborating with Firmus, Sharon AI, IREN, ResetData, Megaport (via Latitude.sh), CDC, NEXTDC and AirTrunk to expand land, power and shell capacity for multiple generations of NVIDIA DSX AI factories - 'up to a 2-gigawatt buildout by 2027'. Sharon AI deploying up to 68,000 NVIDIA GPUs; IREN applying the DSX blueprint to its 800 MW Bundey campus (SA); Firmus expanding Project Southgate; CDC quoting >550 MW operating across AU/NZ with 800 MW under construction and zero-water cooling 'certified for NVIDIA accelerated computing infrastructure'; NEXTDC operating 'AI factories built on NVIDIA DSX'; AirTrunk expanding direct-to-chip liquid-cooled powered shells; ResetData citing Australian data residency for government customers. Named model users: Heidi, Atlassian. Read in full (chunks 0-1); chunk 2 is NVIDIA boilerplate. Announced eight weeks after the PM's national AI standards speech and is the direct hardware-to-Australia mapping the thread exists to track.

sources.title: AI in Australia's interests - speech by the Prime Minister, University of Sydney, 15 July 2026
sources.notes: Announces mandatory 'Australian Standards for AI': a single national framework absorbing the March 2026 expectations for large AI data centres, covering where they are built and the power and water they use; National Cabinet agreement sought August 2026; legislation to Parliament 'early next year'. Legal obligation on next-generation large-scale data centres to underwrite new power supply, pay their full share of grid connection, and be net generators ('put at least as much energy into our grid as they take out'); minimise water use, maximise energy efficiency, pay for additional water infrastructure. Sovereignty framing: refusing to be 'a data warehouse for AI products made overseas' and warning against 'subcontracting our sovereignty and security to the control of foreign monopolies'; AI named 'a critical - and urgent - innovation priority for our defence force and security agencies'.

sources.title: Revealed: Australia's $100 million investment in controversial tech giant Palantir (Crikey, 29 January 2026)
sources.notes: Future Fund held 498,339 Palantir shares valued at $103,649,987 as of 30 June 2025 (citing the FF periodic report); $1,616,512.92 in February 2023 (citing an FF disclosure PDF); <$25m in December 2024 (citing Deepcut News). The stake is larger than the fund's holdings in AGL, Seek or NEXTDC. Also records: Palantir's US$30m ICE contract for ImmigrationOS; 404 Media's reporting on the ELITE tool using Medicaid data; the 2024 Defence contract (CN4104368) being for Foundry per FOI-obtained emails. The FF December-2025 figures superseded by SRC_FF_PIR_DEC25 (primary).

sources.title: Defence signs biggest ever contract with Palantir for department's 'Cyber Warfare Division' (Crikey, 17 February 2026)
sources.notes: Defence's total Palantir spend 'more than $26 million ... since 2013' per Crikey's analysis of AusTender. Describes CN4218984 as a limited tender ('land and expand'); quotes Senator David Pocock: 'deeply problematic for millions of Australian taxpayer dollars to be going to a company that is so mired in controversy' and 'terrible procurement process'. States the Cyber Warfare Division previously held a one-year $4.1m software deal running until December 2025 and a $7.15m contract in August 2024. Also states: 'In November 2024, the Australian Signals Directorate granted the firm a top security clearance' - the date conflicts with Palantir's own IRAP PROTECTED announcement of 20 Nov 2025 (RG-089); and names Palantir's Australian customers as ASD, ACIC, Coles, Westpac and Rio Tinto. Neither Defence nor Palantir responded to Crikey.

sources.title: From ICE to Coles: Controversial US tech company Palantir's links to Australia spark backlash (Crikey, 8 July 2025)
sources.notes: Australian government clients named with AusTender links: Department of Defence (CN4115523), ACIC (CN3996124), ASD (CN3992202). Corporate clients: Coles (citing iTnews), Rio Tinto (citing International Mining), Westpac (citing a LinkedIn post by a Palantir APAC executive - weak evidence, RG-088). Records Senator David Shoebridge (Greens digital rights spokesperson) calling for a freeze on government contracts with Palantir and quoting his demand for procurement guidelines 'that prevent public money being handed to companies actively engaged in genocide and suppressing democracy'; embeds his 7 Jul 2025 Bluesky thread ('multiple Defence contracts worth over $11 million'). Also records the UN Special Rapporteur report naming Palantir, Palantir's ImmigrationOS work for the Trump administration's deportation agenda (citing Biometric Update), and 12+ former employees protesting (citing NYT, 30 May 2025).

sources.title: As top AUKUS official joins Palantir, ethics watchdog warns of lobbying 'risks' (Crikey, 5 September 2025)
sources.notes: Damian Parmenter CBE, the UK's former Director General for AUKUS (2023 to February 2025), joined Palantir in July 2025 as 'senior counselor' and London-based 'international defence and security adviser'; his own description (via ACOBA) includes 'international opportunities within Europe and the Indo-Pacific'. Palantir says he will comply with ACOBA conditions including a two-year lobbying moratorium. His LinkedIn does not mention the AUKUS role.

sources.title: Business Appointment Application: Damian Parmenter CBE, former Director General, AUKUS, Ministry of Defence. Paid appointment with Palantir Technologies UK, Ltd (ACOBA advice letter, June 2025)
sources.publisher: UK Advisory Committee on Business Appointments
sources.notes: Read in full. ACOBA findings: Parmenter 'stepped back' from DG AUKUS on 1 February [2025]; Palantir attended his AUKUS outreach events; as DG Delivery and Strategy he visited Palantir 'to understand its work supporting Ukraine'; the proposed role provides 'decision support' to the UK Head of Palantir 'focused on international opportunities within Europe and the Indo-Pacific'. The Committee: 'it is likely that Mr Parmenter would have amassed a network of contacts while in office especially in the US and Australia by virtue of his role at AUKUS ... there is a risk these contacts ... may be seen to offer new business development opportunities for Palantir'. Conditions imposed: no use of privileged information; two-year bar on lobbying the UK government, on using in-office contacts to advantage Palantir, on advising Palantir on UK government/MoD bids, and on lobbying contacts made in office 'in other governments and organisations'. A primary-source document of a UK ethics regulator assessing the AUKUS-to-Palantir revolving door, naming Australia as the risk surface.

sources.title: Dozens of government insiders lobbying for defence industry, analysis shows (ABC News / Four Corners, 23 August 2026)
sources.publisher: ABC News (Mark Willacy, Lesley Robinson, Dylan Welch, Samantha Dick)
sources.notes: Four Corners analysis identifies at least 60 former defence ministers, senior officers and officials who moved into weapons firms or lobbying companies. Directly relevant: 'Mike Kelly, a Labor defence materiel minister in 2013, served as the Australian president of the controversial US software and intelligence company Palantir from 2020 to 2024.' Christopher Pyne (former defence minister, now lobbyist): his firm is 'number one in defence'; 'there's $368 billion being spent on AUKUS over the lifetime of the agreement'. Senator Shoebridge: 'AUKUS is like a feast. It's this multi-billion-dollar feast for lobbyists ... In a $400 billion program, there are entire careers'. Also records Maj Gen Jeremy King's move to Lockheed Martin ANZ within a week of leaving the ADF, after involvement in the $2.8bn Black Hawk purchase.

sources.title: EXCLUSIVE: Pentagon to adopt Palantir AI as core US military system, memo says (Reuters, 20 March 2026)
sources.notes: Read in full. Deputy SecDef Steve Feinberg's 9 March 2026 letter makes Palantir's Maven Smart System an official program of record - 'locks in long-term use of Palantir's weapons-targeting technology across the U.S. military'; Maven described as already 'the primary AI operating system for the U.S. military, which has carried out thousands of targeted strikes against Iran over the last three weeks'; oversight moves from NGA to the Pentagon CDAO, future contracting via the Army. History: began as a 2017 drone-imagery labelling program; 2024 contract worth up to $480m; May 2025 ceiling raised to $1.3bn; separate Army deal 'worth up to $10 billion' announced the previous summer; market value 'nearly $360 billion'. Records the UN expert warning on AI targeting without human intervention and Palantir's position that humans approve targets. Also notes Maven's use of Anthropic Claude and the Pentagon's supply-chain-risk designation of Anthropic (March 2026).

sources.title: U.S. Army Awards Enterprise Service Agreement to Enhance Military Readiness and Drive Operational Efficiency (US Army release, 31 July 2025)
sources.notes: Primary confirmation (via search abstract; article text not archived) of the Army-Palantir enterprise agreement: consolidates 75 contracts (15 prime, 60 related) into a single agreement. Corroborated by DefenseScoop and Breaking Defense (31 Jul - 1 Aug 2025): 10-year deal worth up to $10bn. Figure used in metrics as REPORTED with the corroborating coverage named here; upgrade to VERIFIED requires reading the army.mil article in full.

sources.title: 'Growing demand' sparks DOD to raise Palantir's Maven ceiling above $1B (DefenseScoop, 23 May 2025)
sources.notes: The initial $480m five-year IDIQ for Maven Smart System was inked May 2024; the ceiling was raised to $1.3bn in May 2025. Corroborates Reuters' contract history; search-abstract level reading (full text not retrieved).

sources.title: 'The Business of War': Google Employees Protest Work for Pentagon (New York Times, 4 April 2018)
sources.notes: Project Maven's origin event: thousands of Google employees signed a letter asking the CEO to pull out of the project that could improve drone-strike targeting; Google declined to renew and adopted AI principles (corroborated by Arms Control Association, Jul 2018). Palantir became a follow-on Maven integrator. Search-abstract level reading (paywalled full text not retrieved); the fact recorded is the protest and its outcome, both stated in the abstract.

sources.title: New strategic partnership to unlock billions and boost military AI and innovation (UK Ministry of Defence release, 18 September 2025)
sources.publisher: UK Ministry of Defence / John Healey MP
sources.notes: Read in full. Signed by Defence Secretary John Healey. Palantir to invest up to £1.5bn in the UK, make London its European defence HQ, create up to 350 jobs (up to 200 Palantir + 150 wider sector); identifies UK Defence opportunities 'worth up to £750 million over the next five years'. The release itself describes the work as supporting the 'kill chain' - fusing open-source and military data 'to provide military commanders with faster options for attacking an enemy target' - as an element of the Digital Targeting Web from the Strategic Defence Review, with capabilities 'already being proven on the battlefield in Ukraine' and ensuring 'data remains sovereign'. Karp: up to £750m 'invested in the most advanced AI-enabled defence technology, honed on the battlefield in Ukraine and used extensively by the US and NATO ... our largest presence outside of the US'. A Five Eyes government's own primary description of Palantir's defence-AI role - the strongest sourcing for the 'weaponisation' premise, and a contrast case for what Australia has NOT published about its own Palantir use.

sources.title: UN report lists companies complicit in Israel's 'genocide': Who are they? (Al Jazeera, 1 July 2025)
sources.notes: Coverage of UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese's report 'From economy of occupation to economy of genocide' (A/HRC/59/23, OHCHR - the underlying primary document was NOT read; this record rests on Al Jazeera's summary). 48 corporate actors named including Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, IBM and Palantir. On Palantir: support to the Israeli military expanded since October 2023; 'reasonable grounds' to believe it provided automated predictive policing technology used for automated decision-making in the battlefield, processing data and generating target lists including through AI systems 'Lavender', 'Gospel' and 'Where's Daddy?'. Also: BlackRock is Palantir's second-largest institutional investor (8.6%), Vanguard the largest (9.1%). The 'automated predictive policing' language is the closest a UN document comes to the brief's 'pre-crime' framing - about battlefield targeting, not street policing.

sources.title: Palantir Achieves Information Security Registered Assessors Program (IRAP) PROTECTED Level, Unlocking New Opportunities in Australia (Palantir investor release, 20 November 2025)
sources.notes: Read in full. IRAP PROTECTED achieved under the Australian Information Security Registered Assessors Program, assessed by an independent third-party IRAP assessor per ASD requirements. KEY RESIDENCY FACT: 'Palantir Platform Australia (PPA) delivers advanced cloud services - including Foundry and AIP - hosted in Australian Amazon Web Services (AWS) regions'. Paul Rawlins quoted as AU Head of Public Sector. This is the company's own primary statement of where its Australian platform data is hosted; whether every Australian deployment (Defence CWD, ASD, ACIC) actually runs on PPA is RG-087.

sources.title: Palantir Platforms (official platform descriptions: AIP, Foundry, Gotham, Apollo)
sources.notes: Retrieved 2026-09-21 (no publication date on page). Official positioning used for the premise checks: AIP - 'Activate and Control AI on Your Private Network'; Foundry - 'The Ontology-Powered Operating System for the Modern Enterprise'; Gotham - 'The Operating System for Global Decision Making ... a commercially-available, AI-ready operating system that improves and accelerates decisions for operators across roles and all domains'; Apollo - 'The Operating System for Continuous Delivery. From the back of a humvee to the hull of a submarine, Apollo enables continuous deployment across all environments.'

sources.title: WA police facial recognition trial launches with a real-time arrest - and backlash over privacy (The Guardian Australia, 20 July 2026)
sources.notes: Read chunk 0 of 3. Australia's first law-enforcement REAL-TIME facial recognition trial: five-month mobile trial from 2 Jul 2026 (Perth, Mirrabooka bus station); live van camera scanning hundreds of faces a minute against a database of ~4,000 people (outstanding warrants, registered child sex offenders, missing persons); a live arrest occurred during the launch media conference. Week one: 130,000+ faces scanned, 33 alerts, 19 arrests, two welfare checks, 21 registered sex offenders 'engaged with', two acknowledged false alerts, 'human in the loop'. OIC WA (state privacy regulator) was not consulted and warns of 'collective privacy harms' (statement PDF on wa.gov.au). Commissioner Col Blanch: 'This is not about mass surveillance ... less of an intrusive capability than a standard CCTV camera.' 2026 Australian Community Attitudes to Privacy Survey: 45% of Australians consider facial recognition the biggest privacy risk (up from 27% in 2023). NO vendor named - the technology is NOT attributed to Palantir anywhere in the reporting (RG-093).

sources.title: NSW Police face questions on use of facial recognition algorithm from 2011 (Biometric Update, 5 November 2025)
sources.notes: NSW Police used Cognitec's FRT algorithm from 2011 to early 2025 inside the PhotoTrac Suspect Identification System, operated by State Intelligence Command's Facial Recognition Unit and the Real Time Intelligence Centre; never contracted support or updates; also ran NYX, adapted in-house from Google's open-source FaceNet, from 2018. Discontinuation reportedly cost-driven; media and a Greens MP had linked it to demographic-accuracy concerns. Cognitec supplying algorithms to Australia's major international airports. Grade C: trade press, but its claims are attributed to a Cognitec email and named prior reporting.

sources.title: Rio Tinto to extend use of Palantir Technologies' AI-based solutions (International Mining, 14 November 2024)
sources.notes: Read in full. Rio Tinto renewed its multi-year Palantir enterprise agreement for a further four years, securing ongoing access to AIP; early Foundry adopter. Australian operations named: the RTIO Operations Centre in Western Australia coordinates 53 driverless iron-ore trains (240 wagons each) across the Pilbara network through Foundry's Ontology; Oyu Tolgoi (Mongolia) geotechnical risk. Quotes Rio Tinto CCO Bold Bataar and Palantir Head of Commercial Ted Mabrey. The largest Palantir commercial deployment touching Australian industrial operations on the public record.

sources.title: Coles Group is making big strides with its advanced analytics (iTnews, 18 November 2024)
sources.notes: Read chunk 0 of 5. At Coles' investor day, COO/supply-chain chief Matt Swindells detailed the Palantir partnership (announced earlier in 2024 as running the Palantir analytics suite across its supermarkets): executive oversight and workforce management; 24,000 process 'standards' used 'to run a Coles shop in a week ... measured to 15-minute increments'; effectiveness of directed in-store activity claimed to rise from 15% to 70% through data-guided tasking. The workforce-management dimension matters for the surveillance question: this is data about 100k+ workers' movements and tasks, not customer facial data.

sources.title: All the Ways Palantir is Assisting Trump's Abusive Removal Campaign (ACLU, 24 March 2026)
sources.publisher: American Civil Liberties Union (Sophie Feng, Jay Stanley)
sources.notes: Read chunk 0 of 4. ACLU's consolidated account: ELITE (Enhanced Leads Identification and Targeting for Enforcement) maps deportation targets with 'address confidence scores', draws on HHS, USCIS and Thomson Reuters CLEAR data, and is used to find 'target rich' locations (per 404 Media's obtained user guide and ICE court testimony on 'immigration nexus' counts); the Investigative Case Management platform as ICE's backbone (per The Intercept and DHS's own privacy impact assessment); ACLU's 2018 reporting on Palantir-built New Orleans predictive policing with 'threat scores'; Amnesty International calling for Palantir to cease the work. Advocacy source with documented primary underpinnings; graded B, and the ELITE/ICM specifics are attributed to the named investigations rather than asserted here.

sources.title: We're All So F'd | NVIDIA x Palantir, Global Surveillance, 'Pre-Crime' Arrests, & AI (GNCA Investigates, YouTube)
sources.notes: The originating framing for this research thread: its description states Jensen Huang said NVIDIA would 'accelerate everything that Palantir does' (a paraphrase of the verified GTC DC keynote quote - see SRC_SHERWOOD_GTC_QUOTE and RG-092). Approximately 489k views and 44k likes as at 2026-09-21; publication date estimated December 2025 from contemporaneous archive posts (Lemmy, 21-22 Dec 2025) - the exact date was not read from YouTube. A follow-up channel video ('Palantir Crashes Out in Response to GN', youtube.com/watch?v=5Idb_D4Tdu8) reports a response from Palantir's Head of Strategic Communications. entities.name: Palantir Technologies Inc.
entities.notes: NYSE: PLTR. Denver-headquartered data analytics and AI software company; co-founded by Peter Thiel and others. Platforms: Gotham ('operating system for global decision making' - defence/intelligence positioning), Foundry (enterprise Ontology OS), Apollo (continuous delivery across environments, 'from the back of a humvee to the hull of a submarine'), AIP (AI on private networks). US defense record: Maven Smart System program of record (Mar 2026); $480m IDIQ May 2024 raised to $1.3bn May 2025; Army enterprise agreement up to $10bn (Jul 2025, consolidating 75 contracts); ICE ImmigrationOS/ELITE/ICM. Named in UN Special Rapporteur report A/HRC/59/23. NVIDIA partnership from 28 Oct 2025. Australian subsidiary: Palantir Technologies Australia Pty Ltd.

entities.notes: ABN 48 144 948 309 (as published on AusTender notices). Registered supplier address Canberra ACT 2601. regulatory_events.summary: Prime Minister announces mandatory 'Australian Standards for AI': a single national framework covering large AI data centres' locations, power and water use, absorbing the March 2026 expectations for large AI data centres; National Cabinet agreement sought for August 2026; legislation planned for early 2027. Next-generation large-scale data centres to be legally obliged to underwrite new power supply, pay their full share of grid connection, be net generators of energy, minimise water use and pay for additional water infrastructure. Speech also names AI 'a critical - and urgent - innovation priority for our defence force and security agencies' and warns against 'subcontracting our sovereignty and security to the control of foreign monopolies'.
regulatory_events.outcome: Framework announced; National Cabinet and legislation pending as at Sep 2026.
regulatory_events.notes: event_type 'other' because the vocabulary has no 'framework_announced' value and forcing 'rule_change_request' would misstate a government announcement as a request. Recorded in this thread because it is the policy frame into which NVIDIA's up-to-2GW Australian AI-factory buildout landed eight weeks later (9 Sep 2026), and because its net-generator and water obligations interact directly with the observatory's existing consent-condition findings.

research_gaps.question: Establish whether any Australian law-enforcement or criminal-justice agency runs Palantir software, and for what: what the ACIC's 'Software Maintenance & Support' contract actually supports; whether any state police force, Home Affairs/ABF or AFP holds a Palantir deployment (state portals, not just AusTender); the vendor of the WA Police real-time FRT trial; and the current tooling of the NSW Police Real Time Intelligence Centre post-Cognitec.
research_gaps.why_it_matters: The brief asserts 'facial recognition and pre-crime arrest capabilities' as a partnership consequence. The verified Australian picture is different and must stay different until evidenced: live-FRT arrests are happening (WA, from July 2026) with NO vendor named; NSW Police ran a 2011-vintage Cognitec algorithm plus in-house FaceNet-derived NYX; the ACLU-documented Palantir policing tools (NOPD threat scores, ICE ELITE/ICM) are American. If Palantir software ever touches an Australian police watchlist or fusion system, that is a material new fact; the absence of such evidence today is also a fact, and the gap says which.
research_gaps.target_source: buy.nsw / Buying for Victoria / QTenders searches (Palantir, ABN 48144948309); WA Police FRT trial disclosures and OIC WA correspondence; ACIC annual reports and FOI; NSW Police FOI on PhotoTrac/SIS successor tooling; AFP and Home Affairs procurement plans
research_gaps.notes: Strict separation rule for this thread: no row may link Palantir to an Australian policing capability without a primary source. The WA trial row carries no vendor attribution and must not gain one by inference.
